own_solution.law: Timoshenko bimetal curvature with m=1: kappa = 24 dAlpha dT / (h [12 + (1+n)(1+1/n)]); delta = kappa L^2/2
assumptions: small curvature, linear elastic, perfect bonding

defect_reasons.other: Which layer is on top is not stated, so only the magnitude of the deflection is fixed; also the quantity label for TE1D7/TC665 ('a further length of strip') actually describes tape length, a metadata mislabel that does not affect any answer.

notes: Checked: kappa = 24*4.2e-4/(16.5*1e-3) = 0.61091 1/m; base 12.218 mm; L=26 cm: 20.649 mm; L=31 cm: 29.354 mm; L=35 cm: 37.418 mm, all matching the certified answers. Width cancels (moment and stiffness both proportional to width). Minimal pairs hold: T374D vs T1A9F differ only in timing (earlier experiment vs just before measurement), same 11 cm; TE1D7 vs T9949 differ only in the object pulled out (tape vs strip), same 11 cm. Numeral-free twins T90F6 and TC665 match their D twins' wording. Agrees with pass 1.
